name: Duskwell Mood Gels — Calm Amber
description: Translucent amber soft-gel capsules — officially a 'functional confection' — containing bioactive serotonin-pathway modulators that produce a mild, 90-minute calm without sedation. Sold in blister packs of 12. Flavor is honey-chamomile with a faint black pepper finish.
flavor_profile: Warm honey and dried chamomile sweetness, slightly floral, with a barely-there black pepper prickle that signals the bioactives are active; smooth gel texture
slogan: Calm is a choice you can make.
cultural_context: Duskwell Calm Amber occupies a contested cultural space — some users treat them as necessary coping tools in a high-stress city, others see them as corporate emotional management. Tier 2 workers buy them in bulk. There is an active debate about whether employers can require employees not to take them on shift.
story_hooks: A Helion Health internal memo suggests that Calm Amber's bioactive formula subtly increases compliance with authority figures during the 90-minute window — the memo is real, and someone wants to get it out.
A character discovers that a family member has been taking Calm Amber daily for two years — far beyond recommended use — and is now experiencing emotional flatness that looks like depression.
A Tier 1 underground lab is producing unlicensed Calm Amber knockoffs with a stronger formula and selling them at Φ3.00 a pack; the formula has no safety ceiling built in.
